predecessors.name: Warring States Japan
predecessors.text: the Date ancestral lands: Date City, Kawamata, Kōri and Kunimi

ledger.x: 1584: Masamune 'succeeded Terumune as head of the Date clan'; the ancestral lands are named on the page (Date City, Kawamata, Kōri, Kunimi); Date district was awarded to Isa Tomomune in 1189.

1584: retainer Ōuchi Sadatsuna defected to the Ashina clan of the Aizu region and Masamune declared war; the Nihonmatsu fell in 1585-1586 and Masamune 'effectively won a series of battles' against the Sōma and Ashina in 1588.
1589: Kurokawa, the Battle of Suriagehara against the Ashina, Sukagawa against the Nikaidō.

1589: 'Masamune seized the Aizu Domain of the Ashina at the Battle of Suriagehara and installed himself at Kurokawa Castle'; the Masamune page: 'sealed the Date clan's hegemony over southern Mutsu Province'.

1591: Masamune 'forfeited the Date ancestral lands' (Date City, Kawamata, Kōri, Kunimi) to Hideyoshi, 'which caused riots', and 'never regained them'; the Yonezawa Domain page: Hideyoshi 'moves the Date clan to Iwadeyama' and gives the Gamō Aizu.
1591-1601: after the Kunohe Rebellion Masamune 'received Iwatesawa and rebuilt it as Iwadeyama Castle'; he stayed 13 years.
1600: Ieyasu awarded Masamune the Sendai Domain; established 1600.
1601: Aoba Castle becomes the Date base of power; 1604 the move to Sendai village with 52,000 vassals.
1868: Sendai sponsored the Ōuetsu Reppan Dōmei after Sendai men killed the Chōshū officer Sera Shūzō in May 1868; 'the focal member of the Ōuetsu Reppan Dōmei against the Meiji Restoration'.
After the Boshin War 'Sendai's holdings were reduced'.
1871: the domain 'was dissolved in 1871 under the abolition of the han system'; the Date clan page: 'ruled until 1871'.

wars.name: Date–Ashina war and the conquest of southern Mutsu
wars.outcome: The Nihonmatsu surrendered in 1585 and Terumune was killed; Hitotoribashi (January 1586); Kōriyama (1588); Kurokawa and Suriagehara against the Ashina (1589); the Date held southern Mutsu.

wars.name: Siege of Shiroishi and Hasedo
wars.outcome: Masamune fought for the Tokugawa eastern army at Shiroishi and Hasedo during the Sekigahara campaign and was awarded the Sendai Domain.

wars.name: Boshin War (Ōuetsu Reppan Dōmei)
wars.outcome: Sendai was the focal member of the northern coalition against the restoration; its holdings were reduced afterwards.

certainty.note: The pages name castles, battles, towns and koku, not borders; the Date holdings are a circle at the start and the Fukushima and Miyagi prefectures later.
